Definition: from another form of G3178; to drink to intoxication, i.e. get drunk:--drink well, make (be) drunk(-en).
BiblicalUsage: Paul says one man at the Lord's table is hungry while another is drunken, warns that the drunken are drunken in the night, and Peter answers the crowd at Pentecost that the disciples are not drunken. John adds the wedding at Cana, where men have well drunk before the good wine is served. The word is drinking to excess, and Scripture ties it to the night and to shame.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that drunkenness is the opposite of watchfulness: the night is when men get drunk, and the morning of Pentecost is when God pours out His Spirit on sober men. The morning of Pentecost belongs to sober men, and the Spirit fills those who watch.
